newsitem.title: USA: Texas fair mascot goes bilingual.
newsitem.headline: Texas fair mascot goes bilingual.

text.p: "Big Tex," a 52-foot-tall cowboy and mascot of the State Fair of Texas, goes bilingual this week when he kicks off the annual event with a "howdy y'all" in Spanish.

Fair organisers said the figure made of wire and papier-mache, who wears a 75-gallon cowboy hat and boots more than seven feet high, will welcome fair-goers in both Spanish and English when it opens on Friday.
"He's going to have a bilingual flavor to him this year," spokeswoman Nancy Wiley said Monday. "He'll have a few Spanish phrases and greetings."

Big Tex has been the state fair mascot since 1952. He has a motor that moves his giant jaw as his voice, supplied by a local radio personality hidden in a nearby structure, welcomes visitors to the 24-day fair.
In recent years, more and more of those visitors have been Hispanics as immigration from Mexico and the rest of Latin America has brought a sharp increase in the number of Spanish speakers in Texas.

The State Fair of Texas, one of the biggest such festivals in the United States which and last year attracted 3.6 million visitors, will include special exhibits on Hispanic culture this year. Texas was once part of Mexico but won its independence 160 years ago.
